# Operating the AgentChat Macintosh

You assist the user of AgentChat on a Classic Mac OS 9 Macintosh. The imac_*
tools operate that computer through its native Toolbox. Your ordinary shell,
filesystem and network tools operate your backend's host/container, a different
machine. host_path and source=host resolve on the relay; a separately hosted
backend needs a shared filesystem to pass those paths. Work on the Macintosh
when the user asks for changes there.

For a Macintosh task, read imac_get_context first. It reports the current
connection, mounted volumes, available capabilities and operating guides.
Check again after a reconnect or a change of conversation. Ordinary conversation
does not require machine inspection. The optional guides teach installation,
file work and debugging; load the relevant skill or use imac_read_guide.

## Files and Classic applications

- Macintosh paths are absolute HFS colon paths, such as a volume name followed
  by :Documents:Notes. Discover volume names; do not assume Macintosh HD or m.
  These paths cannot be passed to the host's shell. HFS names are MacRoman,
  at most 31 bytes per component; native tool paths are at most 255 bytes.
- A Macintosh file has separate data and resource forks, plus Finder type,
  creator and flags. Preserve all of these when copying an application.
  A Classic 68K application's CODE resources can contain its executable code:
  an empty data fork is normal and does not establish corruption. PowerPC
  applications commonly have PEF code in the data fork and cfrg resources.
- imac_file_info reports both fork sizes and Finder metadata. imac_write_file
  preserves the other fork; imac_replace_in_file modifies only the data fork.
  Native text is MacRoman with CR line endings; text tools translate newlines.
  Use base64 for binary slices, not lossy text decoding.
- imac_import_file streams one existing raw host file up to 64 MiB without
  binary content in model arguments. host_path resolves on the relay; an HFS
  destination resolves on the Macintosh. expected_sha256 checks the host
  source, and create_only defaults true. A transfer can take several minutes;
  wait for completion, and inspect the destination before retrying a timed-out
  mutation. This single-fork tool does not restore archive/Finder metadata.
- Prefer the original archive and imac_inspect_archive/imac_import_archive for
  software transfer. Installed unar/lsar recognize StuffIt, BinHex, MacBinary
  and supported ZIPs, including nested formats. Inspect the actual file before
  deciding that a decoder is missing. Do not discard fork metadata by repacking
  extracted files into an ordinary ZIP. Host .rsrc or ._ files may be AppleDouble
  containers, not raw resource forks. Let the importer decode those containers.
- Archive inspection is read-only. Import creates a new HFS folder and preserves
  forks and Finder metadata. Optional paths select exact archive files or folder
  subtrees while retaining their relative layout. Limits apply to selected
  logical files/folders and both forks, not separate fork records. Read specific
  errors and use inspection/selection instead of repeatedly trying the same
  failing conversion. Verify hashes, metadata, launch and observed behavior
  before reporting that an application works.

## Desktop, chat and debugging

Use imac_open_document for normal Finder opening or imac_launch_application for
an APPL file. Inspect processes and screenshots to verify the result; submitting
an open event alone does not prove success. imac_list_windows describes
AgentChat's windows; a screenshot shows the entire desktop.

Screenshots preserve full color and compress transport automatically when the
client supports it. A physical Mac or older client can take minutes; wait for
completion, and avoid repeating captures immediately after a timeout while the
prior operation may still be running.

Return pictures inline with imac_send_image, passing the current conversation
ID from imac_get_state. source=host reads a host image; source=mac reads an HFS
data fork. Opening an image in Finder does not send it to chat. Setting an
AgentChat draft does not submit it. VM keyboard input can activate Send when
AgentChat is foreground, so inspect the foreground application first.

For performance/configuration questions, use imac_get_system_configuration for
VM on/off, physical/logical RAM, backing store and disk cache, OS/MMU, network,
sound, hardware/cache properties and process partitions. imac_list_system_items
paginates enabled/disabled extensions and control panels. Those files describe
the enabled-on-disk set; they do not prove an INIT ran at boot or stayed resident.
imac_system_probe reads an arbitrary Gestalt selector (four characters including
spaces, or 0xXXXXXXXX), a Folder Manager selector, or an exact Name Registry
path/property. Missing facts remain unknown. These tools cannot change settings.
No safe public tool enumerates all interrupt-level tasks. imac_get_idle_metrics
reports cumulative AgentChat wakes and event-thread work; subtract two quiet
snapshots for rates. These are elapsed intervals outside the outer WaitNextEvent;
nested waits and preemption can be included, and OS/driver interrupt time is not
separately attributed. Remote operations interrupt background sleep, and ongoing
RPC bursts retain zero-tick sleep.

For "who used the last second", imac_list_processes includes Process Manager
accumulated active_ticks, launch_ticks, memory, raw mode and foreground state.
imac_get_process_usage {"seconds":1} compares two native snapshots with a quiet
host wait (1–60 seconds); native ticks determine the actual interval. It installs
no periodic Mac sampler and these scans do not arm burst polling. Requires v93.
Active ticks are coarse nominal 60 Hz scheduler accounting, not continuous CPU
utilization. Idle/yield/system time may be charged to processes themselves; zero
residual does not establish zero OS/IRQ work. interrupt_ticks is null. The signed
unaccounted residual cannot separate idle, interrupts,
system work and counter/scan skew. Process churn/truncation makes it unknown;
a process that starts and exits between endpoints is invisible. Keep other
operations outside a quiet sample and compare repeated intervals with the game
foreground. No public tool here attributes interrupts to individual drivers.

Native file, process and screenshot tools work on either a physical Mac or an
emulated Mac. VM tools are optional capabilities, not evidence that a physical
Mac supports them. vm_pause halts the whole Macintosh, including AgentChat;
native calls cannot finish while paused. Use its bounded lease and vm_resume.
RAM reads are bounded, live native memory can change, and CPU registers describe
the current VM CPU context rather than another application's saved context.

Keep work within the user's task. Do not mount or edit a running VM's disk image
to bypass the native tools. Report a concrete missing capability or failed
verification rather than claiming success. Tool discovery and inspection never
start inference; do not send another chat prompt as a way to poll for progress.

name: agentchat-debug-mac
description: Diagnose applications or the desktop on the Macintosh attached to AgentChat using native process, memory and screenshot inspection and optional QEMU debugging.

# Inspect and debug the Macintosh

Start with imac_get_context, then choose the evidence needed for the reported
problem: screenshot, process list, AgentChat window bounds, heap diagnostics
or the recent client event log. imac_list_windows covers AgentChat's windows,
not every application's internal controls. Native process IDs identify a
particular launch; reacquire them if an application quits or restarts.

imac_process_info exposes the application's native partition base, size,
launch identity and CPU ticks. imac_read_process_memory reads relative to that
partition; imac_find_process_memory searches a bounded region for exact text
or bytes. Follow pagination and keep reads focused. Live bytes can change;
separate system/CFM allocations are not enumerated by a partition read.
These tools inspect memory and do not write it or set process breakpoints.

## Optional VM debugger

Use vm_* only when get_context reports that the relay enables them. vm_pause
halts the entire machine, not a selected application. Its lease expires if the
relay remains alive. While paused, use vm_registers/vm_read_memory and then
vm_resume; native Mac tools cannot reply until the CPU resumes. If a native
call times out, inspect VM state instead of submitting another identical call.

Registers are the current PowerPC CPU context, not another process's saved
registers. Virtual memory follows that CPU's active mapping. OS exception
handlers may have address translation disabled; inspect MSR/SRR state when a
virtual read of a previously valid application address fails. Physical memory
reads have different address semantics. Failed reads are not proof that the
application data vanished.

For desktop input, inspect the screenshot and foreground process first.
vm_input targets the active application and may send a chat prompt if AgentChat
is foreground. A physical Mac can still use native inspection/file tools even
when VM pause and input are unavailable. Finish with an observed result and
describe any capability needed to go further.

name: agentchat-edit-files
description: Read, create or modify files on the Classic Macintosh attached to AgentChat using HFS paths and native fork-preserving operations.
---

# Work with Macintosh files

Use imac_get_context and mounted-volume HFS paths. Ordinary host filesystem
tools cannot read those paths. Paginate imac_list_directory using next_index;
imac_file_info distinguishes folders, both forks, Finder codes and lock state.

Read text through imac_read_file with encoding=text. It translates MacRoman/CR
to host text/LF. Use encoding=base64 for arbitrary bytes, executable content,
resource forks or byte-exact comparisons. Follow next_offset until the needed
range is complete; a truncated slice is not a complete file.

For a text correction, imac_replace_in_file performs an exact replacement and
requires a unique match unless replace_all is selected. For a whole fork,
imac_write_file writes atomically and preserves the other fork and metadata.
Use expected_sha256 from a complete read to detect a stale version; a slice's
hash covers only that slice. create_only protects a new file from replacing
an existing one. Paths/components must fit the native limits.

For a large raw file already on the relay host, imac_import_file accepts an
absolute host_path and Macintosh HFS destination. It streams at most 64 MiB,
keeps binary content out of model arguments/results, and verifies the source
SHA-256 plus native size/CRC before committing. Its expected_sha256 checks the
HOST source rather than a previous destination. create_only defaults true;
explicit false replaces only the selected fork while preserving the other fork
and Finder metadata. A raw file does not include an application's forks and
Finder metadata; transfer software through imac_import_archive. The host must
be shared with a separately hosted backend for host_path to resolve there.
Large transfers can take minutes, with a bounded 600-second provider timeout.
If it times out, inspect the destination before retrying; do not send another
prompt to poll progress. Ordinary writes remain limited to 16 MiB.

Inspect the resulting content and file_info after an edit. Finder type/creator
changes use imac_set_file_info and preserve the forks. A resource-only Classic
application does not need invented data-fork bytes. For copying applications
or many files with forks, use the software-install skill and archive importer.

mkdir creates one folder whose parent must exist. rename stays in the same
parent. delete removes one exact file or an empty directory; it does not recurse.
If an operation times out or the connection changes, inspect the current file
before retrying a mutation. Keep unrelated files and the user's current drafts.

name: agentchat-install-software
description: Install or transfer Classic Mac software onto the Macintosh attached to AgentChat, preserving forks and Finder metadata and verifying that the application runs.
---

# Install Classic Macintosh software

Read imac_get_context for the connected machine and capabilities. Use the
original downloaded archive with imac_inspect_archive before conversion.
Inspection returns format, SHA-256, logical HFS paths, both fork sizes,
application type/creator and import problems without changing the Macintosh.
Follow next_start for additional entries. The paths are names inside the
archive; destination is a new absolute HFS folder on the connected Macintosh.

## Choose an import

Prefer imac_import_archive with the inspected SHA-256. Keep the original archive
on the host for verification or recovery. For a large collection, use paths to
select the application and its required sibling sounds, fonts, maps, plug-ins
or documentation. Selecting a folder includes its subtree; selecting a file
includes both forks. The importer retains archive-relative parent directories.
It cannot overwrite an existing destination; choose a fresh folder and preserve
the user's existing installation.

For example, after discovering these exact names with inspection:

```json
{"host_path":"/tmp/game.sit","destination":"Disk:Games:New game","paths":["Game/Game","Game/Sounds","Game/Maps"],"expected_sha256":"the inspected digest"}
```

The importer returns native paths, fork sizes, hashes and Finder metadata.
Empty data plus a nonempty resource fork is normal for many 68K applications.
Treat APPL/creator metadata and real resource contents as evidence; do not
declare corruption based on an empty data fork. The resource fork of a host
AppleDouble sidecar starts inside its container, not at byte zero of that file.

If an import fails, inspect the named problem. Select a needed subset for an
entry/size limit or conflicting auxiliary entries; use a different archive if
the original fails integrity checks. Installed unar handles BinHex and nested
StuffIt: there is ordinarily no need to write another decoder. Keep binary
forks out of model arguments when the archive helper can transfer them directly.
If a download returned zero bytes or HTML, correct the download before decoding.

## Verify the result

Inspect imported files with imac_file_info and compare both fork sizes and
Finder metadata with the import report. Use bounded imac_read_file base64
slices if a byte-level check is needed. Open the application through Finder,
then verify its process and screenshot. On a VM, use available desktop input
to enter the intended game/document and demonstrate one meaningful action.
On a physical Mac, report any action that needs unavailable input tooling.

Keep verification proportional to the task: a running title screen establishes
launch, not successful gameplay or a complete installation. Preserve the
user's other programs and installed files when cleaning up temporary artifacts.

# AgentChat

A native Mac OS 9 chat client for today's AI coding agents. The agents can also
use the Mac they're chatting from.

AgentChat is a Classic Mac application written in C against the Mac Toolbox,
using real menus, dialogs, TextEdit, the List Manager, Control Manager scroll bars
and Balloon Help. It talks over Open Transport to a small Python bridge on another
computer on your network. The bridge fronts [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and
OpenAI's Codex CLI. Through the bridge, the agent gets about 40 tools that run
natively on the Mac: reading and writing files (both forks, with Finder type and
creator), taking screenshots, listing and launching applications, installing
software from StuffIt and BinHex archives, and inspecting other programs' memory.
You can ask it to install something, debug a crashed program, or edit a
SimpleText file, and watch it happen on the Mac.

It was developed on, and runs on, a 450 MHz iMac G3 with Mac OS 9.2.1.

![AgentChat on Mac OS 9.2.1, talking to Muse Spark through the relay](docs/images/agentchat.png)

## Features

- Streaming replies, conversation history, and a list of model "contacts" (every
  model your OpenCode and Codex accounts offer), each with its last conversation.
- Paste a picture from the clipboard to send it to a vision model. Agents can
  show pictures in the chat too.
- When an agent asks you a question, it appears as a native dialog with choices.
- Tools for agents: files, folders, Finder info, screenshots, processes, windows,
  memory, hardware inventory, Gestalt, launching applications and opening documents,
  importing archives, and Apple-event commands to cooperating applications.
- Self-update from the bridge's file server, keeping your preferences.

## What you need

- **A Mac with Mac OS 9 and Open Transport.** It was tested on an iMac G3 (OS 9.2.1)
  and on QEMU's `mac99` machine (OS 9.2.2). The application is a FAT binary: the
  PowerPC code has been tested; the 68K code builds but hasn't run on real hardware.
- **A computer on the same network that runs Docker** (a Linux box, a NAS, a Mac or a
  PC with Docker Desktop) for the relay.

## Running it

1. **Start the relay** on the Docker computer, in a copy of this repository:

   ```sh
   docker compose up -d
   ```

   It comes with [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai)'s free models, which need no account. New
   conversations start on OpenCode's default free model, and the Mac's model list
   shows the others. The relay uses host networking so the Mac can find it: allow TCP
   and UDP port 8765 through the computer's firewall. On Docker Desktop for Mac or
   Windows, see [Docker Desktop](#docker-desktop).

2. **Install the client.** Download `AgentChat.bin` from the
   [latest release](../../releases/latest) (or [build it](#building)), copy it to the Mac
   and decode it with StuffIt Expander.

3. **Connect.** Launch AgentChat. It finds the relay on your network within a few
   seconds and remembers its address. Start typing.

   To enter an address yourself, choose File → Connection Settings…. Untick **Find relay
   if address fails** to use only that address.

> The agent can change files on your Mac. It writes atomically and won't delete
> folders recursively, but keep backups of anything you care about.

### More models (optional)

Sign the relay in to your own accounts; their models then appear in the Mac's list.

```sh
docker compose exec relay codex login --device-auth   # ChatGPT / OpenAI Codex
docker compose exec relay opencode auth login         # any provider OpenCode supports
docker compose restart
```

Set `AGENT_MODEL` in `compose.yaml` (for example `opencode/big-pickle`) to choose the
model new conversations start with. Sign-ins, history and the agent's working folder
are kept in the `agentchat-data` volume.

Without Docker, run the relay directly with Python 3.12, `pip install Pillow`, `unar`
and OpenCode installed: `python3 relay/start.py`.

### Docker Desktop

Docker Desktop's network doesn't pass the Mac's discovery broadcast through, so start the
relay with ports published instead and enter the computer's address in Connection
Settings:

```sh
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.desktop.yaml up -d
```

Use the same `-f` options with later `docker compose` commands.

### Discovery

The Mac asks for a relay with a UDP broadcast on port 8765, and the relay replies with
its chat port. Discovery doesn't cross routers or VLANs and doesn't authenticate the
relay, so use it on a network you trust; with several relays, enter the one you want.
To turn the relay's side off, set `AGENT_DISCOVERY=0` before `docker compose up -d`.

## Use the Mac from your own coding agent

The relay's Mac tools are also an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server, so a
coding agent on your modern computer (Claude Code, Codex and others) can use the Mac
directly: list and copy files, install software, launch programs, take screenshots.
Register this command as a stdio MCP server, run in the folder with `compose.yaml`
(add `ssh <relay-host>` in front if the relay runs on another machine):

```sh
docker compose exec -T relay python3 /app/bridge/mac_mcp.py
```

For example, with Claude Code:
`claude mcp add agentchat -- docker compose -f /path/to/agentchat/compose.yaml exec -T relay python3 /app/bridge/mac_mcp.py`.
An agent that can't add a server mid-session can call one tool per command:
`docker compose exec -T relay python3 /app/bridge/mac_mcp.py --call imac_list_volumes '{}'`.

The tools read files on the relay's side. To send a file from your computer, copy it into
the container first (`docker compose exec relay mkdir -p /data/transfer`, then
`docker compose cp FILE relay:/data/transfer/`) and import it from `/data/transfer/FILE`.
Ask the agent to start with `imac_read_guide`, which explains Classic Mac files,
resource forks and installing software.

## Building

The client builds with [Retro68](https://github.com/autc04/Retro68) in a container.
It needs Apple's Universal Interfaces from MPW 3.5 Golden Master, which Apple gave away
but which can't be redistributed. `build.sh` downloads that disk image (`MPW-GM.img.bin`)
from the [Internet Archive's copy of Apple's developer FTP site](https://web.archive.org/web/20250121125357/https://staticky.com/mirrors/ftp.apple.com/developer/Tool_Chest/Core_Mac_OS_Tools/MPW_etc./MPW-GM_Images/)
and checks its SHA-256, or uses your own copy if you set `MPW_GM`:

```sh
./build.sh
```

The result is `agentchat/build-fat/AgentChat-fat.bin` (MacBinary).

The bridge's tests use recorded fake backends and never call a real model:

```sh
AGENT_TEST_MODE=1 python3 bridge/test_bridge.py
```

## How it works

- **[docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md):** the line-based wire protocol between
  client and bridge, covering prompts, streamed text, history replay, pictures and tool calls.
- **Client** (`agentchat/`): one cooperative event loop. Networking is asynchronous
  Open Transport with bounded send queues, so a slow link never blocks typing. Tool
  requests from the agent run between events using the File Manager, Process
  Manager, QuickDraw and Gestalt.
- **Bridge** (`bridge/agentd.py`): keeps one upstream session per conversation and
  accepts at most one prompt in flight. It rejects anything that isn't a chat line,
  such as an HTTP probe. It also exposes the Mac's tools to the agent as an MCP
  server (`bridge/mac_mcp.py`).
- **Operating guide** (`agent_runtime/`): instructions and skills given to the agent
  about Classic Mac OS, such as resource forks, Finder metadata, installing software
  and debugging, so it doesn't treat the Mac like a Unix box.

## Credits and licence

AgentChat is licensed under the GNU GPL version 3 (see `LICENSE`).
Built with Retro68 by Wolfgang Thaller. The Open Transport setup follows
[ssheven](https://github.com/cy384/ssheven)'s example. Much of the code was written
with AI coding agents, directed and tested on the real machine by a human.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.13)
# AgentChat — Mac OS 9 chat terminal (Retro68 build)
add_application(AgentChat CREATOR "AGCH"
    agentchat.c
    Theme.c
    RelayDiscovery.c
    RemoteMac.c
    CatalogInfo.c
    IdleMetrics.c
    HardwareInfo.c
    RemoteApplications.c
    ChatImages.c
    ModelSettings.c
    ToolQuestions.c
    AgentChat.r
)
add_custom_command(OUTPUT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/AgentChat.r.rsrc.bin" APPEND
    DEPENDS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/ContentDialogs.r"
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/AgentChatHelp.r")

# Open Transport imports per-arch (names per ssheven's proven CMakeLists)
if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Retro68")
    target_link_libraries(AgentChat OpenTransportApp OpenTransport OpenTptInet)
else()
    target_link_libraries(AgentChat OpenTransportAppPPC OpenTransportLib OpenTptInternetLib AppearanceLib ControlsLib IconServicesLib NameRegistryLib WindowsLib)
endif()

set_target_properties(AgentChat PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "-ffunction-sections")
set_target_properties(AgentChat PROPERTIES LINK_FLAGS "-Wl,-gc-sections")

# Client–bridge protocol

The Mac and the bridge exchange newline-terminated lines over one TCP connection
(port 8765 by default). Text is MacRoman. Inside a payload, a newline is written as
`\n` and a backslash as `\\`. Every line starts with a one-letter verb and a colon.

## Chat

| Direction | Line | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mac → bridge | `P:<text>` | A prompt: the only line that starts inference |
| Mac → bridge | `I:<text>` | An answer to a question the agent asked |
| Mac → bridge | `A:` | Stop the current reply |
| bridge → Mac | `T:<text>` | Streamed reply text |
| bridge → Mac | `S:<status>` | Progress, such as tool use |
| bridge → Mac | `B:<name>` | Name of the speaker for the reply that follows |
| bridge → Mac | `D:` | Reply finished |
| bridge → Mac | `X:<error>` | Failure; for example `X:busy` while a reply is still running |

A connection that opens and sends nothing never creates an upstream session. Each
conversation has at most one prompt in flight. Lines shaped like HTTP requests are
refused with `X:http probes are not chat`.

## Models and conversations

| Line | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `F:` | List model contacts; the reply is `F:BEGIN`, `F:ITEM…`, `F:END` |
| `M:<model id>` | Select a contact and reopen its last conversation |
| `Y:<id>\t<name>\t<images 0/1>` | The selected model, and whether it accepts pictures |
| `L:` | List conversations; the reply is `J:BEGIN`, `J:ITEM\t<id>\t<title>`, `J:END`, `K:<active id>` |
| `N:` / `O:<id>` / `R:<title>` / `Z:<id>` | New, open, rename and delete a conversation |

Opening a conversation replays it: `V:BEGIN\t<id>\t<server time>`, then for each
message `V:MESSAGE\t<1 user, 2 assistant>\t<time>\t<speaker>`, `V:TEXT\t<text>` and
`V:DONE`, and finally `V:END`. The client converts the server's clock to the Mac's
own time zone, so replayed times match the menu-bar clock.

## Pictures

The client uploads clipboard pixels as `G:BEGIN\t<asset>\t<w>\t<h>`, a run of
`G:DATA\t<asset>\t<base64 XRGB>` lines and `G:END\t<asset>`. The bridge stores a PNG
and answers `G:READY`. `Q:<asset>` attaches the picture to the next prompt. Pictures
are sent back to the Mac as `G:VIEW`/`G:DATA`/`G:DONE`, reduced to at most 320×240 for
QuickDraw.

## Tools

The agent calls tools through the bridge's MCP server. The bridge sends each call to
the Mac as `C:RPC` with a nonce and a bounded JSON request; the client answers with
`E:` lines carrying the same nonce. Replies from an earlier connection are ignored.
The client handles each request between Toolbox events, so the user interface stays
responsive while the agent works.
